text.arabic_uthmani: كَلَّآ إِنَّ كِتَٰبَ ٱلْفُجَّارِ لَفِى سِجِّينٍۢ

words.gloss_range: corrective and deterrent discourse particle; here it opens the ayah by refusing the prior inference before the record is certified

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: annulling emphatic particle beginning the certified replacement clause

words.prose: {{ar:كَلَّآ}} ({{tr:kallā}}) makes the ayah begin as a halt, not as neutral information. It rejects the complacent inference carried over from the prior standing scene (83:6) and then hands the listener to {{ar:إِنَّ}} ({{tr:ʾinna}}), where the replacement fact is certified. The prolongation and doubled center make that refusal linger in recitation, so the disclosure of the wicked record arrives as a rebuke-shaped correction.

topics.headline: the ayah opens by refusing an inference
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the record is introduced as an answer to a stance already being rejected, not as a detached new topic.
topics.reason: QAC and translation support identify the word as a discourse particle of rejection, deterrence, or corrective transition, matching the CRITICAL claim that the ayah opens with rebuttal force.

topics.headline: the halt turns into certified disclosure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the two-step movement: refusal first, then an emphatic clause that installs the corrected fact.
topics.reason: The following {{ar:إِنَّ}} ({{tr:ʾinna}}) clause is strongly licensed as the governing frame for the record and predicate, so the particle can be read as launching correction into certification.

topics.headline: the rejection is audibly held
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the opening refusal as a sustained brake before the certified record clause begins.
topics.reason: The surface includes the recitational prolongation, and no guardrail evidence blocks treating that visible form as supporting the particle's discourse force.

words.gloss_range: annulling emphatic particle; here it governs the record as its accusative subject and certifies the delayed predicate

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the governed accusative record phrase
the emphatic prepositional predicate
emphatic lām reinforcing the predicate phrase

words.prose: {{ar:إِنَّ}} ({{tr:ʾinna}}) installs the corrected statement as an emphatic nominal clause. It governs {{ar:كِتَٰبَ ٱلْفُجَّارِ}} ({{tr:kitāba l-fujjāri}}) and holds the listener in affirmation until the predicate {{ar:لَ فِى سِجِّينٍۢ}} ({{tr:la fī sijjīnin}}) arrives. Because the clause has no finite verb, the record's confinement is presented as a settled status, while the later {{ar:لَ}} ({{tr:la}}) stacks a second emphasis on the same certified fact.

topics.headline: the particle governs the certified record clause
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that certainty is built into the grammar before the place of confinement is even heard.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence strongly licenses {{ar:كِتَٰبَ}} ({{tr:kitāba}}) as the governed accusative subject and {{ar:لَفِى سِجِّينٍ}} ({{tr:la-fī sijjīnin}}) as the predicate.

topics.headline: rebuttal shifts into formal assertion
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the discourse turn from the opening brake into a formal replacement proposition aimed at resistance.
topics.reason: The opening particle is corrective and the current particle begins the emphatic clause, so the CRITICAL sequence of negation plus confirmation is locally coherent.

topics.headline: confirmation has a compressed sound center
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the confirming particle as forceful rather than weightless connective tissue.
topics.reason: The form-specific sound observation supports the same emphatic function already licensed by grammar.

words.gloss_range: record, register, or binding written dossier; here the governed construct head whose location is certified
words.root_gloss_range: broad writing-root range including joining, writing, prescribing, registering, and contractual binding; local grammar selects a record-register while allowing binding and gathered-document pressure

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: definite genitive class specifying the record
predicate location of the record
annulling emphatic particle governing the record
confinement endpoint of the predicate

words.prose: {{ar:كِتَٰبَ}} ({{tr:kitāba}}) is the accusative subject of {{ar:إِنَّ}} ({{tr:ʾinna}}), so the ayah first makes the record, not the people themselves, carry the clause's grammatical burden. In construct with {{ar:ٱلْفُجَّارِ}} ({{tr:l-fujjāri}}), the record is specified as theirs and about them, gathering the class under one documentary heading. The root field of writing, joining, prescription, and registration is locally narrowed to a binding record-register: wrongdoing is not merely narrated, nor is a recorder brought into view, but fixed as an archive whose settled place is {{ar:سِجِّينٍۢ}} ({{tr:sijjīnin}}). This same record word also starts a local thread answered by the marked record in 83:9 and by the righteous-record contrast in 83:18 and 83:20, while the wider judgment-book pattern shifts from exposure in 18:49 to confinement here.

topics.headline: the record carries the clause
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that judgment is staged first through documentation: the record is what the clause locates.
topics.reason: The word is syntactically forced as the accusative governed subject of {{ar:إِنَّ}} ({{tr:ʾinna}}), and the predicate phrase locates that record.

topics.headline: the construct binds class and archive
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees that the wicked are accessed through a specified record relation rather than named as an independent predicate.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence makes {{ar:ٱلْفُجَّارِ}} ({{tr:l-fujjāri}}) the genitive dependent of the construct, so possession, specification, and documentary relation are locally licensed.

topics.headline: writing becomes a binding archive
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the record as fixed, gathered, and binding, while the local noun still selects record-register rather than every branch of the root.
topics.reason: V4 supports writing, joining, prescription, registration, and contract branches for the root, but local grammar and form select the concrete record while preserving binding and gathered-dossier pressure.

topics.headline: the form foregrounds the document, not a scribe
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees that the wording suppresses recording agency and focuses on the existing archival object.
topics.reason: The local form is a concrete noun, not an active recorder form or a passive written-object form, so the document-register is foregrounded.

topics.headline: this record begins a local register contrast
topics.reader_payoff: The reader recognizes the current record as the first node in a same-surah archive thread that continues in 83:9, 83:18, and 83:20.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows provide concrete same-surah references, and the immediate context support warns that 83:8-9 should constrain the reading window.

topics.headline: record language shifts from exposure to enclosure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees a judgment-book pattern specialized here: the record is not opened for confrontation as in 18:49, but located in confinement.
topics.reason: The concrete reference to 18:49 supports comparison, while local syntax narrows the payoff to location and confinement rather than disclosure.

words.gloss_range: the definite plural class of the wicked or boundary-breakers; here genitive within the record construct
words.root_gloss_range: root range includes splitting, bursting, dawn-cleaving, sudden inburst, moral breach, expansive giving, and named violated-sanctity battle-days; local form selects the moral breach class while preserving rupture imagery

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: construct head whose genitive dependent specifies the record
confinement endpoint that reverses the rupture-class image
construct phrase in which the class appears through its record

words.prose: {{ar:ٱلْفُجَّارِ}} ({{tr:l-fujjāri}}) names a definite plural class, but it is grammatically genitive inside {{ar:كِتَٰبَ ٱلْفُجَّارِ}} ({{tr:kitāba l-fujjāri}}), so the people enter the clause through their record. The root's physical field of splitting, gushing, and dawn-cleaving is narrowed here to moral breach, while the intensive plural form makes the breach a settled class identity. That matters because the clause answers outward rupture with enclosure: the boundary-breakers' record is certified as being in {{ar:سِجِّينٍۢ}} ({{tr:sijjīnin}}), and the same class label recalls judgment contrasts such as 82:14 and 38:28.

topics.headline: the class defines the record from inside the construct
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the wicked are not the sentence subject; their class is routed through the record that names their fate.
topics.reason: The word is syntactically forced as the genitive second term of the construct, so it specifies the record without becoming the clause's subject.

topics.headline: rupture becomes habitual class identity
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the moral label as boundary-breaking identity, while physical gushing and dawn-cleaving remain imagery rather than selected local senses.
topics.reason: V4 supports multiple root branches, but the local active-participle-like plural selects the moral breach branch while keeping rupture imagery as local color.

topics.headline: boundary-breaking is answered by enclosure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the central irony: those named by breached limits have their record placed in a confinement word.
topics.reason: The record phrase containing the rupture-class is predicated into {{ar:سِجِّينٍۢ}} ({{tr:sijjīnin}}), making the claimed reversal locally grammatical and semantically coherent.

topics.headline: the class label returns in judgment contrasts
topics.reader_payoff: The reader connects this class label with nearby and cross-surah judgment contrasts, especially 82:14 and 38:28, while seeing this ayah specialize it through the record.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL evidence gives concrete references for the recurring class label, and local grammar narrows the comparison to the record-location staging in 83:7.

words.gloss_range: emphatic predicate lām attached to the following preposition; it reinforces the certified location without adding a new argument

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: preposition fused with the emphatic lām in the predicate onset
annulling emphatic particle paired with the predicate lām
fused emphatic-location surface formed from lām plus preposition

words.prose: {{ar:لَ}} ({{tr:la}}) is the emphatic lām at the start of the predicate phrase, not a possessive or purposive particle. Its force is inseparable from {{ar:فِى}} ({{tr:fī}}): the fused surface {{ar:لَفِى}} ({{tr:la-fī}}) makes the record's containment sound certified rather than merely located. After the construct phrase is complete, this short particle marks the turn into the predicate and stacks with {{ar:إِنَّ}} ({{tr:ʾinna}}) as double confirmation.

topics.headline: the lām intensifies the predicate
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the location phrase is not neutral; it is the insisted content of the certified clause.
topics.reason: QAC identifies the particle as emphatic and attachment evidence makes the following phrase the predicate of {{ar:إِنَّ}} ({{tr:ʾinna}}).

topics.headline: certainty and location are fused in one onset
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears emphasis carried directly into the containment preposition, rather than as a detachable extra particle.
topics.reason: The input aligns {{ar:لَ}} ({{tr:la}}) and {{ar:فِى}} ({{tr:fī}}) separately while noting their fused surface in the predicate phrase.

topics.headline: the predicate turn carries double confirmation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the clause shift from naming the record to insisting where it is, with confirmation at both the opening and predicate.
topics.reason: The lām is licensed inside the predicate of the {{ar:إِنَّ}} ({{tr:ʾinna}}) clause, so stacked emphasis is local rather than a separate proposition.

words.gloss_range: preposition of containment or inclusion; here it governs Sijjīn and forms the emphatic predicate locating the record

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: genitive object of the preposition
emphatic lām fused with the preposition
annulling emphatic particle whose clause takes the prepositional predicate

words.prose: {{ar:فِى}} ({{tr:fī}}) keeps the record and {{ar:سِجِّينٍۢ}} ({{tr:sijjīnin}}) distinct: the record is inside Sijjīn, not identical with it. As the preposition governing the final noun, it turns containment into the predicate of the whole {{ar:إِنَّ}} ({{tr:ʾinna}}) clause. Its fusion with {{ar:لَ}} ({{tr:la}}) makes that containment emphatic, while the place-like and register-like senses remain jointly useful until 83:9 specifies the marked record.

topics.headline: containment is the predicate
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the sentence is completed by being-inside, not by an action or simple description.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence forces {{ar:سِجِّينٍۢ}} ({{tr:sijjīnin}}) as the object of the preposition and the resulting phrase as the predicate.

topics.headline: the preposition prevents identity collapse
topics.reader_payoff: The reader keeps the record and Sijjīn distinct while still allowing Sijjīn to feel like both place and domain.
topics.reason: The grammar locates the record in the named domain; it does not make the record itself identical with that domain.

topics.headline: the location is certified by the fused lām
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the move into confinement as both grammatical completion and emphatic assertion.
topics.reason: The preposition appears with emphatic {{ar:لَ}} ({{tr:la}}), so its locative government is also the certified predicate onset.

words.gloss_range: Sijjīn as a named confinement domain or register; here the genitive endpoint of the emphatic predicate
words.root_gloss_range: root range centers on imprisonment, confinement, prison-place, captive state, and the named Sijjīn domain; reviewed side branches are not locally active

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: preposition governing Sijjīn as the predicate object
record whose endpoint is Sijjīn
rupture-class whose record lands in Sijjīn

words.prose: {{ar:سِجِّينٍۢ}} ({{tr:sijjīnin}}) is the final genitive object of {{ar:فِى}} ({{tr:fī}}), so it completes the predicate rather than modifying the record. The name gathers prison-place, custody, and register pressure: the record is not merely associated with judgment, but put inside a marked confinement domain within the order just framed by the standing before the Lord (83:6). Its rare intensified form, doubled center, long vowel, and tanwīn make the endpoint heavy and technical, while 83:8 immediately turns the same name into a question and 83:9 answers with a marked record. The word also reverses the motion of {{ar:ٱلْفُجَّارِ}} ({{tr:l-fujjāri}}): the boundary-breakers' archive lands in a word of enclosure, with the broader prison field recalling the contrast of 12:33.

topics.headline: the final noun completes the predicate
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the whole emphatic clause lands only when the final confinement name is heard.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence makes the word the governed object of {{ar:فِى}} ({{tr:fī}}), and the prepositional phrase supplies the predicate of the clause.

topics.headline: Sijjīn is both confinement place and record domain
topics.reader_payoff: The reader keeps both sides alive: Sijjīn feels like a prison-domain and, in view of 83:9, a register tied to a marked record.
topics.reason: V4 supports confinement and the named Sijjīn branch, and translation support warns that 83:8-9 should constrain over-specific translation.

topics.headline: prison language is borrowed onto the archive
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the document itself treated as held under restraint, while the local grammar keeps the record as the thing located, not a human prisoner.
topics.reason: The root family supports confinement and custody imagery, but the subject located is {{ar:كِتَٰبَ}} ({{tr:kitāba}}), so the prison field is applied to an archive.

topics.headline: the rare intensified name resists plain prison gloss
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the endpoint is a marked technical name, not an ordinary prison noun.
topics.reason: The local form is tagged as a proper-name-like noun, V4 lists Sijjīn as a named lower confining place, and contextual evidence marks the exact form as low-occurrence.

topics.headline: closure becomes the next ayah's question
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the final word as both the endpoint of 83:7 and the object that 83:8 immediately asks about.
topics.reason: Translation support explicitly notes that 83:8 asks about Sijjīn and 83:9 supplies the compressed answer.

topics.headline: the rupture class closes in enclosure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the ayah's closure as a reversal: the record of boundary-breakers ends in a confinement name.
topics.reason: The local phrase binds the rupture-class to a record and then predicates that record into Sijjīn, supporting the semantic and sound reversal.

topics.headline: the prison field recalls 12:33
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the prison field can reverse from chosen refuge in 12:33 to imposed archival confinement in 83:7.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows give 12:33 as a concrete prison-field comparison; local syntax keeps the comparison at the level of prison imagery rather than identical scene function.

topics.headline: the name sounds pressed and held
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the doubled center, long vowel, and final release as matching the word's constricted semantic load.
topics.reason: The sound observations reinforce the confinement payoff already licensed by root and predicate evidence.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **A record that binds breaches into confinement.** `ك ت ب` B002 supplies a written record, `ف ج ر` B004 supplies departure from right and breach of restraint, and `س ج ن` B001 supplies confinement. The spatial construction `لَفِى` places the record “in” confinement, while 83:9 specifies it as marked. I assign writing the role of joining dispersed acts into one inspectable object and confinement the role of preventing their escape from attribution. The abductive move is that recording fixes what breach attempted to let flow beyond bounds. The ayah reads as a reversal: boundary-breakers acquire a bounded record.

2. **A binding decree about enrolled offenders.** `ك ت ب` B003 supplies decree and judgment, while B004 supplies inscription into a register or group. The collective `ٱلْفُجَّارِ` and later parallel record of the righteous (83:18) activate the register sense. I infer that the “book” is both evidence and status assignment. The ayah therefore preserves a juridical reading alongside the material written-record reading.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: The elevated parallel book in 83:18–20 and the return question in 83:36 revealed that confinement is one outcome within a symmetric record-system, not the record's inherent character.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **A record that is already a binding judgment.** Lexical evidence: ك ت ب/B002, "joining letters into writing," and B003, "inscribing as binding decree or judgment," in كِتَٰبَ; س ج ن/B001, "confinement in a place of detention," in سِجِّينٍ. Structural cue: 83:4-6 supplies summons and standing, while 83:9 calls the book marked and 83:11 names reckoning. Assigned role: B002 makes conduct legible; B003 makes the inscription operative; confinement gives the operative direction. Abductive move: I infer that record and sentence are fused rather than merely adjacent; the nominal syntax supplies containment, not an explicit causal verb. Reading change: كِتَٰبَ is not a neutral archive awaiting judgment but a dossier whose inscription has binding force.

2. **Boundary-breaking answered by containment.** Lexical evidence: ف ج ر/B004, "departure from right and breach of restraint," in ٱلْفُجَّارِ; س ج ن/B001 in سِجِّينٍ. Structural cue: their earlier transaction crossed the recipient's due boundary (83:2-3), and 83:12 later names overstepping through ع د و/B001. Assigned role: breach describes the agents' outward motion; prison supplies the spatial inverse that stops it. Abductive move: I infer a measure-for-measure reversal from the juxtaposed branch images; the packet does not explicitly say confinement is caused by boundary breach. Reading change: the ayah becomes a spatial correction in which those defined by bursting restraints meet a record held inside restraint.

3. **Enrollment fixes a formerly advantageous identity.** Lexical evidence: ك ت ب/B004, "inscribing someone into a register or group," in كِتَٰبَ, with the group noun ٱلْفُجَّارِ. Structural cue: 83:2-3 showed agents switching standards with transactional position; 83:9 gives the register a fixed mark. Assigned role: enrollment removes role-switching by assigning the agents to the class produced by their practice. Abductive move: I infer that repeated conduct is the enrollment criterion; no explicit registrar is named. Reading change: the "book of the boundary-breakers" reads as the act by which fluid marketplace advantage hardens into accountable identity.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 83:12 supplied the unexpectedly exact spatial counterpart: مُعْتَدٍ names overstepping just after the boundary-breakers' book is confined. This confirmed that س ج ن/B001 is not incidental location but a reversal of ف ج ر/B004 breach.

concept_map.definition: Bir şeyi başka bir şeye katıp aralarında fiziksel ya da topluluk oluşturan bir bağ kurmaktır. Derileri dikme, açıklıkları bağlama veya kapatma ve insan ya da atları düzenli bir birlik hâline getirme bunun yapıya bağlı gerçekleşmeleridir.

facets.statement: Temel işlem, bir şeyi başka bir şeye katarak ikisini bir bütün veya bağlı bir düzen içinde birleştirmektir.

concept_map.definition: Harfleri çizgiyle düzenleyerek yazılı bir metin oluşturmak ve bu işlemin ürünü olan metin ya da yazılı sayfadır. Birine yazdırma, ondan yazmasını isteme ve yazmayı öğretme ise belirli yapılara bağlı uzantılardır.

facets.statement: Temel işlem, harfleri yazıyla düzenleyip bir metin oluşturmak veya var olan metni kopyalamaktır.
İşlemin ürünü, yazılmış metin veya üzerinde bu metnin bulunduğu sayfa ya da kitaptır.
Bir metni başkasına söyleyerek yazdırmak ve birinden kendisi için yazmasını istemek yapıya bağlı ettirgen ve isteme kullanımlarıdır.
Yazmayı öğretmek, yazı öğretmeni ve öğretim yeri anlamları yazı edinimi alanındaki bağlı kullanımlardır.
Öğretim yerindeki çocuklar veya onların topluluğu için kullanılan biçim, yeri değil öğrencileri gösterir.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar yazmayı harfleri çizgiyle bir araya getiren işlem olarak sunar; yazılı ürün, kopyalama, dikte ettirme, yazma isteği ve öğretimle ilgili kullanımlar bu merkeze bağlanır.

facets.statement: Bir işi yapılması gereken bağlayıcı bir yükümlülük olarak belirlemek temel değerlerden biridir.
Bir konuda geçerli ve kesinleşmiş hüküm vermek aynı belirleme çekirdeğinin yargısal yönüdür.
Bir olayın payını, ölçüsünü veya gelecekte gerçekleşecek sonucunu önceden belirlemek yazgı yönünü oluşturur.

facets.statement: Kişinin adını bir kayıt veya listeye geçirerek ona kayıtlı kişi konumu vermek dalın çekirdeğidir.
Adı pay, geçim tahsisatı veya yönetim siciline yazdırmak resmî kayıt alanındaki özel gerçekleşmedir.
Bir kişiyi tanıklar gibi belirli bir topluluğun içinde saymak, sicile almadan üyelik vermeye uzanan kullanımdır.

identity_judgment.boundary_note: Dal, her türlü yazılı sözleşmeyi değil, bedelin ödenmesiyle özgürlüğe götüren bu özel sözleşme türünü kapsar.

facets.statement: Sahip ile köleleştirilmiş kişi arasında, kişinin kendi özgürlük bedelini ödemesini konu alan özel bir sözleşme kurulur.
Bedel belirlenmiş ödeme dilimlerine bağlanır ve köleleştirilmiş kişi bunu kendi kazancından karşılar.
Kararlaştırılan bedelin tamamlanması sözleşmenin sonucu olarak köleleştirilmiş kişinin özgür olmasını sağlar.
İlgili biçimler sözleşmenin kendisini, sözleşmeye bağlı köleleştirilmiş kişiyi ve bağlama göre sözleşmenin öteki tarafını gösterebilir.
